name: Deliver preconstruction services under a CM agreement
summary: When an owner hires a construction manager during design, the contractor's preconstruction team advises the owner and architect stage by stage until the construction price is agreed. At each design stage the estimator prices the drawings, the project manager reviews constructability, the scheduler and VDC coordinator update the schedule and models, and the preconstruction manager reconciles the numbers with the owner's cost consultant and proposes value engineering when the estimate exceeds the budget. Once design is far enough along, trade packages are tendered and the estimator builds a guaranteed maximum price for owner approval. The process is slow because each stage waits on the consultant's drawings and on owners' funding decisions, and error-prone because estimates are made on incomplete design and must be reconciled with another estimator's numbers.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B annual revenue and a central preconstruction team that serves regional operations.
baseline.notes: Describes CCDC 5A/5B construction management and progressive design-build preconstruction phases in 2019-2022, with estimates in spreadsheet-based estimating software and models in Revit and Navisworks.

unit_of_work: one preconstruction engagement, from the signed preconstruction agreement to an agreed construction price
trigger: The contract award process signs a CM or progressive design-build agreement that includes a preconstruction phase.
end_state: The owner signs the construction-phase price or GMP amendment and the project is handed to the operations team, or the engagement ends because the owner cancels or does not convert.

volume.seasonality: Little seasonality; starts follow negotiated awards, which peak in spring.

evidence.note: One to two new engagements a month, each lasting about 8 to 14 months, gives 10 to 20 engagements running at once, which matches the organisation file's 10 to 22 project-months of preconstruction a month.

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Kick off preconstruction with owner and consultant
steps.description: The preconstruction manager opens the preconstruction job, sets up the project folders and cost codes, and holds a kick-off meeting with the owner and prime consultant to confirm scope, budget, design schedule, estimate stages and reporting dates.

evidence.note: CM engaged during design as owner's advisor on cost, constructability and schedule; durations are estimates.

steps.name: Benchmark the owner's budget against the program
steps.description: The estimator builds a Class D estimate from the functional program using cost per square metre from comparable projects in the cost database, adds escalation and soft-cost allowances, and reports whether the budget fits the funding approval.

error.defect_description: Benchmark projects not comparable (region, building type or year), biasing the budget check.

evidence.note: Pre-design Class D / Class 5 estimate from the functional program; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Walk the site and existing facilities
steps.description: The superintendent drives to the site, walks the existing building or land with the owner's facility staff, and records access, crane positions, utilities, hazardous materials and phasing constraints for an occupied facility.

control.basis: Owner's site-specific orientation and hazard assessment for visitors (infection control risk assessment in hospitals); OHSA general duty of employers

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Prepare master schedule and phasing plan
steps.description: The scheduler builds the preconstruction and construction master schedule in P6 with design stages, approvals, permit dates, trade package tender dates, long-lead procurement and construction phases, and agrees it with the consultant.

evidence.note: Scheduling advice during design is part of CM services; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the consultant's design stage issue
steps.description: The prime consultant develops the next design stage (schematic, design development, or 50% and 90% construction documents) and issues drawings and specifications to the owner and construction manager.

error.defect_description: Package issued incomplete or uncoordinated between disciplines.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Log and distribute the design package
steps.description: The preconstruction manager logs the drawing and specification list, sets the estimate and review due dates and distributes the package to the estimator, project manager, scheduler and VDC coordinator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Take off quantities and price the stage estimate
steps.description: The estimator measures quantities in the takeoff software, prices each element and trade division with current unit rates and trade input, adds general conditions, escalation and design contingency, and compares the total with the previous stage.

error.defect_description: Quantity or scope missed, or design contingency set too low for the stage.

evidence.note: Construction cost estimate at each design stage in elemental and trade format; hours are estimates for a $30-80 million building.

steps.name: Review the design for constructability
steps.description: The project manager assigned to the job marks up the drawings for buildability, sequencing, material choices, long-lead items and coordination gaps between disciplines, and writes the comments log for the consultant.

evidence.note: Constructability advice and requests for trade-specific packages and alternatives; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Run model coordination and clash review
steps.description: The VDC coordinator federates the consultants' models, runs clash detection between structure and building services, and records clashes and missing information for the design team.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Update the schedule for the design stage
steps.description: The scheduler updates the master schedule with the latest design, approval and procurement dates, and flags package tender dates and long-lead items that are now at risk.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Chief estimator reviews the stage estimate
steps.description: The chief estimator checks the estimate's quantities, rates, contingency and escalation against the cost database and the previous stage, and returns it for correction when changes are unexplained.

control.basis: Estimating department review policy: senior estimator sign-off on estimates issued to clients

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Reconcile the estimate with the owner's cost consultant
steps.description: The preconstruction manager and estimator meet the owner's quantity surveyor, compare the two estimates element by element, explain variances and agree adjustments before the numbers go to the owner.

evidence.note: Alberta's cost consultant reconciles its estimates with the construction manager's at each stage and explains elemental variances of 10% or more; durations are estimates.

steps.name: Present estimate, schedule and value engineering options
steps.description: The preconstruction manager presents the reconciled estimate, schedule and risks to the owner and consultant, compares the total with the construction budget and tables value engineering options from the log.

next.condition: estimate over budget or owner asks for options

evidence.note: CM advises the owner and recommends corrective action when the estimate exceeds the budget; the 45% over-budget share is an estimate.

steps.name: Run a value engineering workshop and reprice options
steps.description: The estimator and the design team work through the value engineering log in a workshop, price each option with its effect on schedule and life-cycle cost, and issue a priced options list for the owner's decision.

evidence.note: Three-day value and risk workshops at schematic design and design development in Alberta's schedule of services; durations are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for owner decision on budget and design direction
steps.description: The owner compares the estimate with its funding approval, accepts or rejects value engineering options, and may need board or ministry approval before the consultant starts the next stage.

next.condition: design complete enough to tender trade packages
project cancelled or deferred for funding

evidence.note: Four to five estimate stages from pre-design to 100% documents; the loop probability gives about 2.9 design stages after the initial benchmark.

steps.name: Define trade packages and scopes
steps.description: The preconstruction manager splits the work into 20 to 35 trade packages, writes the scope sheet, inclusions, exclusions and interface notes for each, and sets the tender list from prequalified trades.

error.defect_description: Scope gap or overlap between packages.

evidence.note: Work packages prepared by the CM with the owner and design team and bid by individual trades; package count and hours are estimates.

steps.name: Tender trade packages and level the bids
steps.description: The estimator issues the packages through trade tendering, answers trade questions, and receives and levels the bids for scope so each package has a recommended low compliant trade.

error.defect_description: A trade exclusion is missed in levelling.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Wait for owner and consultant review of trade awards
steps.description: The owner and consultant review the bid tabulations and recommendations and approve trade awards or ask for a package to be retendered or reduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Build the construction price or GMP proposal
steps.description: The estimator totals the approved trade prices, self-performed work, general conditions, contingency, allowances and fee into the construction price or guaranteed maximum price, with the clarifications and assumptions list.

error.defect_description: Allowance or contingency inconsistent with the clarifications.

evidence.note: CCDC 5B conversion to a guaranteed maximum price or stipulated price once design and procurement are advanced; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Operations manager approves the GMP and risk
steps.description: The operations manager who will deliver the project reviews the price, contingency, schedule and clarifications against the project risk register and approves it within delegated authority or escalates it.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: operations sign-off on guaranteed prices

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Present and negotiate the construction price with the owner
steps.description: The preconstruction manager presents the GMP, schedule and clarifications to the owner and consultant, answers questions and negotiates contingency, allowances and exclusions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Wait for owner approval of the price amendment
steps.description: The owner takes the construction price to its board, ministry or lender for funding approval and signs the amendment converting the agreement to the construction phase, or asks for revisions.

next.condition: owner does not convert and tenders or terminates

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Hand over to the operations team
steps.description: The project manager holds the turnover meeting, receives the GMP breakdown, trade bids, design packages, schedule and preconstruction correspondence, and starts project startup.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

exceptions.name: Estimate over budget
exceptions.description: At one or more design stages the estimate exceeds the construction budget and a value engineering workshop is held before the owner decides how to proceed.

exceptions.name: Estimate returned by chief estimator
exceptions.description: The chief estimator returns a stage estimate for correction at least once during the engagement.

exceptions.name: Trade package retendered
exceptions.description: Bids for a package come in over the carried amount or with too few bidders, and the owner asks for it to be rescoped and retendered.

exceptions.name: Project cancelled or not converted
exceptions.description: The owner defers the project for funding or does not accept the GMP, so the construction manager is paid for preconstruction only.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from signed preconstruction agreement to agreed construction price
benchmarks.population: Canadian CM preconstruction phases on institutional buildings, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Built from four to five estimate stages (Alberta schedule of services) at roughly two to three months each including owner review, plus trade tendering and GMP approval; no published duration was found.

benchmarks.unit: cost estimates (Class D, C, B, 50-90% CD, 97-100% CD)

evidence.note: Stages listed in the schedule of services; the CM prepares a matching estimate at each.

pain_points.description: Each design stage waits weeks for the consultant's drawings and then for the owner's funding decision, and the preconstruction team cannot speed either.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; owners compare budgets with funding approvals, as the organisation file notes.

pain_points.description: Two estimators price the same drawings (the construction manager and the owner's cost consultant), and reconciling them takes meetings at every stage.

evidence.note: Reconciliation of CM and cost consultant estimates required at each stage.

pain_points.description: Estimates on incomplete design swing between stages, which triggers value engineering rounds that redo design and repricing work.

evidence.note: CM recommends corrective action when the estimate exceeds the budget; more design options are requested.

pain_points.description: Packaging the work for sequential tenders creates scope gaps and overlaps between trade packages that surface later as change orders.

evidence.note: Difficulty defining the scope of packages for contractors performing work for more than one trade.

sources.title: Practice Tip PT.23.2: CCDC Construction Management Contracts (version 2.1)
sources.supports: Under CCDC 5A and 5B the CM advises the owner and design team during design on constructability, estimated construction costs and scheduling; the CM's services can include preparing or confirming the Construction Cost Estimate at each phase of design and recommending corrective action when it exceeds the Construction Budget; work is split into packages bid by individual trades, some before construction documents are complete; under 5B trade contractors become the CM's subcontractors (often CCA 1); the cost-plus 5B can later be converted to a guaranteed maximum price or stipulated price once design and procurement are further advanced; under 5B the consultant certifies payment for construction but not preconstruction services; the CM often asks for trade-specific drawing packages and proposes substitutions.

sources.title: Schedule of Cost Services for Construction Management (CM) Project Delivery Method
sources.publisher: Government of Alberta, Infrastructure Cost Management
sources.supports: Public owner's cost consultant services on CM projects: estimates at pre-design (Class D / Class 5), schematic design (Class C / Class 4), design development (Class B / Class 3), 50-60% and 80-90% construction documents for each sequential tender package (Class 2) and 97-100% documents (Class A / Class 1); three-day value and risk workshops at schematic design and design development; reconciling the construction manager's estimates with the cost consultant's estimates at each stage; explaining elemental variances of 10% or more against the budget.

assumptions: The organisation file defines the unit of work as one project-month of preconstruction; this file documents one whole engagement instead, because the design-stage loop and the GMP happen once per engagement. One to two new engagements a month lasting 8 to 14 months is equivalent to the organisation file's 10 to 22 project-months a month.
The levelled trade prices from trade tendering are an input inside the engagement, not its trigger; the engagement starts when the preconstruction agreement is signed.
Loaded costs and titles come from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried staff).

Roles needed but not listed for this process in the organisation file: project-manager (constructability and turnover), superintendent (site logistics), chief-estimator and operations-manager (GMP approval).
Monthly preconstruction invoices and progress reports are left out; they are short tasks inside the precon manager's routine.
The design-stage loop is geometric (62% chance of another stage after each owner decision), so a few engagements run many more stages than the typical four.

The simulated median (about 258 days) is below the 300-day estimate because the geometric design-stage loop gives many short engagements and a long tail (p90 about 550 days); both sit within the range of institutional preconstruction phases.
Model coordination, constructability review and schedule updates run alongside the estimate in practice (concurrent_with) but add to the simulated cycle time.
